title: Proactive Spend Sheriff and Topology-aware Allocator for Tenant Budgeting
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers often hit tenant-level spend caps or volatile spot evictions which cause unexpected latency spikes and failed requests. Current routing prefers cheapest available capacity but lacks a tenant-aware enforcement layer that: (1) prevents short-term budget overspend, (2) reasons about spot eviction risk vs. on-demand cost, and (3) selects GPU families that match model requirements (memory, fp precision) while honoring latency SLOs.

This ticket introduces two coordinated components: (A) Spend Sheriff — a per-tenant, time-windowed quota controller that enforces soft and hard budget caps and issues routing hints (throttle, degrade, block) to the allocator; (B) Topology-aware Allocator — a scoring layer that ranks candidate placements by a composite score (expected cost, eviction risk, region proximity, GPU-suitability, current headroom) and applies configurable policies to prefer graceful fallback model variants rather than hard failures. The goal is to reduce surprise customer charges and maintain 99th percentile tail-latency SLAs during cost-constrained conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Spend Sheriff enforces per-tenant hourly and daily soft caps: emits hints when 80% and blocks at hard cap; configurable per-tenant via Console
Allocator scoring uses inputs: per-second GPU cost, spot eviction probability, estimated latency penalty (region hop), and model GPU affinity; results shown in routing decisions logs
Added model-variant fallback policy: if budget-sheriff signals imminent cap breach, allocator prefers pre-validated smaller/quantized variant and records metric showing quality downgrade
Unit + integration tests verifying budget window arithmetic, race conditions under concurrent requests, and deterministic fallback selection
Dashboard with per-tenant spend burn-down, eviction-rate vs decisions, and a golden metric: reduced customer-initiated overage tickets by >= 60% during canary
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout plan executed without customer-impacting errors
design_notes: Spend Sheriff model: sliding-window token accounting aggregated at the tenant-key + billing-rate granularity; soft cap emits 'throttle' hint, hard cap returns 402-equivalent error with structured reason
Score function (topology allocator): score = w_cost*normalized_cost + w_eviction*eviction_risk - w_latency*region_penalty - w_gpu_mismatch*affinity_penalty; weights configurable per-tenant-tier
Eviction risk estimated from recent spot reclaim history + cloud provider forecasts; we store a 12h decay-weighted eviction score per SKU-region pair

GPU affinity: offline profiler maps model variants to preferred GPU family (A100-40 / H100 / RTX-8000) and expected memory headroom; allocator rejects candidates with <10% margin unless fallback variant is available
Fallback variants: maintain a validated list per-model (quantized-int8, window-trimmed, distilled) with expected quality delta and token-rate improvement
Concurrency: use a best-effort reservation token from Sheriff for each request to avoid double-spend between allocator and scheduler; reservations expire in 2s if not confirmed by scheduler
Audit logs: every decision emits structured log: tenant, request_id, chosen_node, score_breakdown, sheriff_state, fallback_used, cost_estimate — used for post-mortem and billing reconciliation
tradeoffs: Aggressive cost weights reduce spend but can increase error rates and lower-quality outputs; must be tunable per tenant to preserve PLG conversion flows
Conservative eviction avoidance increases on-demand spend; we mitigate by limiting on-demand fallback budget via Sheriff policies
Real-time eviction forecasts add complexity but substantially reduce spot-induced p95 latency spikes; fallback needed for forecast errors
Reservation tokens reduce double-spend races but add latency; we limit to 2s to bound tail impact
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated behind tenant opt-in and platform default off
Phase 1 (Canary 1): internal test tenants + 2 low-risk customers (1%) for 72h observing correctness and dashboards
Phase 2 (Canary 2): expand to 10% of customers with medium budgets for 1 week; validate cost savings and no SLO regression
Phase 3: opt-in public beta via Console toggle with clear UI for soft/hard caps and fallback preferences
Full launch: default-enable for P0 and enterprise tiers after 4 weeks of stable telemetry
Rollback: instant disable via FF and immediate reversion to previous allocator; billing reconciliation script to repair any rivered charges

2026-03-13 - QA: Integration tests failing on concurrent accounting race; mitigation added: atomic increment via redis LUA script (PR#1459)
qa_tests: Simulated burst: 10k RPS for 30s on a tenant near soft cap - expect hints at 80% and fallback variant usage without hard errors
Concurrent reservations: 1k parallel requests for same tenant to validate atomic accounting via redis LUA
Eviction forecast error injection: flip eviction score to high mid-request to validate graceful switching and correct charge attribution
Integration with billing: synthetic invoices for affected requests to ensure reconciliation columns populated
